The Ford Mustang family

21 generations and variants in the Index, 1964–present. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 1964½–1973

    Ford Mustang (first generation)

    The original Mustang, 1964½–1973: the car that created the pony-car class, at $2,368, then grew bigger and faster with almost every update.

    271 hp8.2 sec 0-602,981,259 built
    289 V8, 4-speed manual · 390 GT, automatic · Mach 1, 428 Cobra Jet · Boss 351
  2. 1965–1966

    Shelby GT350 (1965–1966)

    The first Shelby Mustang, 1965–1966: a fastback turned into a production-class racer by Carroll Shelby's team in Los Angeles, with 306 hp.

    306 hp6.9 sec 0-602,940 built
  3. 1969–1970

    Ford Mustang Boss 302 (1969–1970)

    The original Boss 302, 1969–1970: a Trans-Am homologation special with high-flow heads, a front spoiler and a rear wing.

    290 hp6.5 sec 0-608,641 built
  4. 1974–1978

    Ford Mustang II (second generation)

    The Mustang II, 1974–1978: smaller, lighter and based on the Pinto, launched just as the fuel crisis hit, and Motor Trend's 1974 Car of the Year.

    105 hp12.2 sec 0-601,107,718 built
    2.8-liter V6, 4-speed manual · Cobra II, 302 V8
  5. 1979–1993

    Ford Mustang (third generation)

    The Fox-body Mustang, 1979–1993: larger than the Mustang II, the 5.0 that made it fast again, and the longest-running Mustang of all.

    225 hp6.3 sec 0-602,518,948 built
    5.0-liter V8, 5-speed manual · 2.3-liter 4-cylinder, 5-speed manual · 1982 GT · 1993 SVT Cobra
  6. 1984–1986

    Ford Mustang SVO

    The SVO, 1984–1986: Ford's racing division's idea of a fast Mustang, with an intercooled turbo 4-cylinder, 4-wheel disc brakes and a European-style chassis.

    175 hp7.5 sec 0-609,844 built
    1984 · 1985½ and 1986
  7. 1994–2004

    Ford Mustang (fourth generation)

    The SN95 Mustang, 1994–2004: rounder styling with cues from the original, Motor Trend's 1994 Car of the Year, the modular V8 and the 'New Edge' restyle.

    215 hp6.1 sec 0-601,562,529 built
    GT, 5.0-liter V8 · 3.8-liter V6, manual · 1999 GT, 4.6-liter V8 · 2003 Mach 1 · 2003 SVT Cobra
  8. 1994–1999

    Saleen S351

    Steve Saleen's answer to the small-block SN95: pull the engine, install a built 351 Windsor, supercharge it to 495 hp by 1999, and serialize it. About 300 exist, the rarest of the 1990s Mustangs.

    495 hp4.6 sec 0-60170 mph top300 built
    S351, 1994 · S351 R-code · S351, 1997–1999 · SR
  9. 2000

    Ford SVT Mustang Cobra R (2000)

    Ford's Special Vehicle Team built just 300 of these stripped, winged, side-piped Mustangs around a hand-assembled 5.4-liter DOHC V8. Loud, heavy and proudly unsubtle, it is a homologation special that would always rather shout than whisper.

    385 hp4.7 sec 0-60300 built
  10. 2005–2014

    Ford Mustang (fifth generation)

    The S197 Mustang, 2005–2014: retro styling from the late 1960s, a new platform, and from 2011 the 412-hp Coyote V8 and a 305-hp V6.

    300 hp4.8 sec 0-601,006,975 built
    GT, 4.6-liter V8 · 4.0-liter V6 · 2008 Bullitt · 2011 GT, 5.0-liter Coyote V8 · 2011 V6, 3.7-liter
  11. 2007–2014

    Shelby GT500 (2007–2014)

    The S197 Shelby GT500, 2007–2014: a supercharged V8 from Ford's Special Vehicle Team and Carroll Shelby, with 500 hp at first and 662 hp at the end.

    500 hp4.5 sec 0-60
    2007–2010, 5.4-liter · 2011–2012, aluminum-block 5.4-liter · 2013–2014, 5.8-liter
  12. 2012–2013

    Ford Mustang Boss 302 (2012–2013)

    The second Boss 302, 2012–2013: a 444-hp Coyote V8, side exhausts, adjustable suspension and a track-ready Laguna Seca version.

    444 hp4.3 sec 0-60
    Boss 302 · Laguna Seca
  13. 2015–2023

    Ford Mustang (sixth generation)

    The S550 Mustang, 2015–2023: independent rear suspension on every car, a turbo 4-cylinder EcoBoost, right-hand drive for export and 3 Shelbys.

    435 hp4.4 sec 0-60668,153 built
    GT, 5.0-liter V8, manual · 2.3-liter EcoBoost · 3.7-liter V6 · 2018 GT, 10-speed automatic · Bullitt
  14. 2015–2020

    Shelby GT350 (2015–2020)

    The S550 Shelby GT350, 2015–2020: a 526-hp flat-plane-crank V8 that revs to 8,250 rpm, a manual only, and the GT350R for the track.

    526 hp4.3 sec 0-60
    GT350 · GT350R
  15. 2020–2022

    Shelby GT500 (2020–2022)

    The S550 Shelby GT500, 2020–2022: a 760-hp supercharged V8, a 7-speed dual-clutch and no manual, the most powerful Mustang until the Dark Horse SC and GTD.

    760 hp3.6 sec 0-60
  16. 2021–2023

    Ford Mustang Mach 1 (2021–2023)

    The Mach 1, 2021–2023: a 480-hp V8 with the GT350's manual gearbox and cooling and suspension parts from both Shelbys, between the GT and the GT350.

    480 hp4.5 sec 0-60
    Tremec 6-speed manual · 10-speed automatic
  17. 2021–present

    Ford Mustang Mach-E

    The Mustang Mach-E, 2021 on: Ford's electric crossover with the Mustang's name, 2 batteries, rear- or all-wheel drive and up to 320 miles of EPA range.

    346 hp4.9 sec 0-60112 mph top210,734 built
    Extended range, all-wheel drive · Standard range, rear-wheel drive · Extended range, rear-wheel drive · California Route 1
  18. 2021–present

    Ford Mustang Mach-E GT and Rally

    The quickest Mach-Es, 2021 on: 480 hp and all-wheel drive in the GT, more torque in the GT Performance Edition, and the Rally, tuned for rough roads.

    480 hp4.3 sec 0-60124 mph top
    GT · GT Performance Edition · Rally
  19. 2024–present

    Ford Mustang (seventh generation)

    The seventh Mustang, 2024 on: a cabin built around screens, a 315-hp EcoBoost, a 480-hp V8 that still offers a manual, and the Dark Horse.

    480 hp4.2 sec 0-6089,336 built
    GT, 6-speed manual · 2.3-liter EcoBoost · GT, 10-speed automatic
  20. 2024–present

    Ford Mustang Dark Horse

    The Dark Horse, 2024 on: the seventh generation's track-focused Mustang, with 500 hp, MagneRide dampers and big Brembo brakes, and 795 hp in the SC.

    500 hp4.1 sec 0-60
    Dark Horse · Dark Horse SC
  21. 2025–present

    Ford Mustang GTD

    The GTD, 2025 on: an 815-hp road car developed alongside the Mustang GT3 racer, finished by hand by Multimatic, and the first Mustang under 7 minutes at the Nürburgring.

    815 hp2.8 sec 0-60202 mph top
